Problem Statement:
Handle unusual __qualname__ in inspect

<!--
Please note that Rich isn't accepting any new features at this point.

If a feature can be implemented without modifying the core library, then
they should be released as a third-party module. I can accept updates to the
core library that make it easier to extend (think hooks).

Bugfixes are always welcome of course.

Sometimes it is not clear what is a feature and what is a bug fix.
If there is any doubt, please open a discussion first.

-->

<!--
*Are you contributing typo fixes?*

If your PR solely consists of typos, at least one must be in the docs to warrant an addition to CONTRIBUTORS.md
-->

## Type of changes

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation / docstrings
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Other

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTORS.md where appropriate (see note about typos above).
- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

I discovered, that an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail.
This can happen if an object is created this way intentionally, but I discovered it, when decorating a class with `@functools.lru_cache` which forwards the underlying attributes using a descriptor when it can't add the to it's `__dict__` because the class uses `__slots__`:

```python
from functools import lru_cache
from rich import inspect


@lru_cache
class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install

    install()

    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```

I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback.

FILES: rich/_inspect.py:103, 254
ROOT CAUSE: The code assumes `__qualname__` is always a string, but it can be a descriptor (e.g., when using `__slots__` with `lru_cache` on a class), leading to a `TypeError` when passed to `Text.assemble` or used in an f-string.
CHANGE: 
1. In `_get_signature`, change `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` to check if the result is a string, falling back to `__name__` and then to a generic fallback.
2. In `get_object_types_mro_as_strings`, ensure `__qualname__` is a string before using it in the f-string.

Specifically for `_get_signature`:
```python
        qualname = getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)
        if not isinstance(qualname, str):
            qualname = getattr(obj, "__name__", name)
        if not isinstance(qualname, str):
            qualname = name or "unknown"
```

Specifically for `get_object_types_mro_as_strings`:
Use a helper or check the type of `getattr(type_, "__qualname__", "")`.

TEST: Run `reproduce_issue.py`.

steps.message:
I have fixed the issue where an unusual `__qualname__` (e.g., a descriptor) would cause `rich.inspect` to fail with a `TypeError`.

Changes:
- In `rich/_inspect.py`, `_get_signature` now verifies that `__qualname__` is a string, falling back to `__name__` or a generic `"unknown"` string if necessary.
- In `rich/_inspect.py`, `get_object_types_mro_as_strings` now also ensures that `__qualname__` is a string before including it in the resulting MRO strings, falling back to `__name__`.

You can verify the fix by running `python3 reproduce_issue.py`.

steps.message: The issue where an unusual `__qualname__` (such as a descriptor when using `__slots__` with `lru_cache`) caused `rich.inspect` to fail with a `TypeError` has been fixed. The fix involves verifying that `__qualname__` is a string in both `_get_signature` and `get_object_types_mro_as_strings`, providing appropriate fallbacks to `__name__` or a generic string. I have verified the fix using a reproduction script.
